map.intent: The map holds the current intents, one per line; git history records how they changed.
Candidates are sibling commits of one base.
The checks are Verus (the spec and proofs) and the tests; a candidate is verified when every check passes and it changes neither the checks, the manifest, nor the map.
A search selects a candidate only when at least two candidates are verified and every verified candidate prints the same output for each agree check.
Among the verified candidates, the highest rank is selected; ties go to the smallest diff.
Trunk fast-forwards to exactly the selected candidate; engineer decides by committing the map and the checks, not by accepting candidates.
Each candidate is written by one process running as user agent in its own working directory, holding one capability.
agent has read and execute permission on the checks, read permission on the transcripts, and no permission on the repository.
No capability is granted until isolation is confirmed.

Each new transcript becomes a proposal: candidates change only the map, each new intent cites its cue, a cue is agreed when at least two verified candidates cite it, and the shortest wording is selected.
Exec code uses the spec's names: each exec type views the spec type of the same name, and the gates are a trait in the spec.
Each trace records every transition under its spec name.

After agreement and before fast-forward, a counterexample search asks other harnesses for a test that splits the agreed candidates; trunk fast-forwards only if no verified test does, and a test that does joins the agreement of the next search for that intent.

Each trace records, for every agent process, its harness, model, tokens, cost and time, and for every check its time and exit status, so that cost per verified candidate = (Σ_c (g(c) + k(c)) + r·t) / v, with r the rate in bon.toml and t the search's wall time.
A blocked search reruns, as wide as bon.toml's width list says for that attempt, until the attempts or a limit run out; only that goes to engineer.
Limits nest like the process tree: each agent process's limit is reserved from its search's, and each search's from the bon process's; wait returns what was unused, and nothing spends past its limit.

A compaction search asks for candidates that remove or simplify code at trunk's head; every verified candidate must print the same as trunk's head on each agree check, and the highest rank is selected.
The SBOM lists every crate, toolchain, TCB tool, service and trusted function bon depends on, as CycloneDX, and a check fails when it differs from the machine.

A skill ships with the CLI for the model engineer talks to: how to work at the spec level and when to run bon, read from the bon.toml, map and spec of the repo it runs in; agent processes never see it.
Trunk is the remote's main: a search starts from it, and every fast-forward is pushed to it, or refused if it moved.
Cost is computed from the harness's token counts and the manifest's prices for the canonical model, and checked against the harness's own figure where it gives one.

A scrub search checks an intent against trunk with tests written from the spec and the intent, never the implementation: an agreed pass lands the test as a check, and an agreed fail marks the intent broken and starts a code search that carries the test.
Counterexample tests are written from the spec and the intent, never from candidate code, and run on every agreed candidate.
Checks start from trunk's build of the protected paths, which no candidate can change.
The device file's jobs caps how many agent processes run at once; width stays what bon.toml says.
Background work, scrub and compaction, runs only on spare capacity, stalest first, staleness being trunk commits since an intent's last scrub or since the last compaction.

fields.doc: The current intents: the map at trunk's head. (intent 1)
fields.name: map

fields.doc: The check paths the manifest declares at trunk's head.
fields.name: checks

fields.doc: Trunk's history; last() is the head.
fields.name: trunk

fields.doc: The git author of each trunk commit, in step with trunk.
fields.name: authors

fields.doc: The bon process's limit, and what it has spent and reserved against it. (intent 16)
fields.name: limit

fields.doc: Outstanding capabilities, keyed by the agent process that holds each. Each is a Verus token: the token is how Verus represents a capability; capability is the term. An agent process holds exactly one, and waiting on it consumes it. (intent 7)
fields.name: capability

items.doc: A git commit, by its hash. (TCB: git)
items.name: Commit

items.doc: A path in a commit's tree, as git reports it. (TCB: git)
items.name: Path

items.doc: One line of the map: what is wanted.
items.name: Intent

items.doc: A WebVTT file, one per recorded call. (TCB: WebVTT)
items.name: Transcript

items.doc: A WebVTT cue, by its start time in milliseconds. (TCB: WebVTT)
items.name: Cue

items.doc: A POSIX user. Names match the users on this machine. Also a commit's git author.
items.name: User

items.doc: The files the policy covers. A directory is a file (OSTEP).
items.name: File

items.doc: POSIX permission bits.
items.name: Permission

items.doc: A process running as agent that writes one candidate: index `index` of the n in search `search`. (OSTEP: process)
items.name: AgentProcess

items.doc: What a search is for: its kind, carrying its goal. Each kind's goal has its own type.
items.name: Kind

items.doc: One generated change, as trusted code observed it after its agent process exited.
items.name: Candidate

items.doc: What an agent process holds to write one candidate.
items.name: Capability

items.doc: One search: n agent processes from one base.
items.name: Search

items.doc: The map's path.
items.name: map_path

items.doc: The manifest's path. It declares the checks, so it is protected like them.
items.name: manifest_path

items.doc: No candidate may change p: the map, the manifest, or a path under a check. A check path covers itself and every path it is a prefix of.
items.name: protected

items.doc: Attenuation at grant: what a capability for this kind may change. (intents 3, 10)
items.name: authority

items.doc: Who may do what. (intent 8)
items.name: policy

items.doc: agent's permissions, as trusted code observed them, match the policy. (intent 9)
items.name: isolated

items.doc: The candidate at index i. Meaningful only when one exists.
items.name: at

items.doc: Passed the vertical bottleneck: every check passes, and every changed path is within the search's authority. (intent 3)
items.name: verified

items.doc: Every agent process has returned.
items.name: complete

items.doc: At least two verified candidates, and every verified pair prints the same. (intent 4) Compaction also measures them against its goal: every verified candidate prints the same as the goal. The goal never votes; it is measured. (intent 17)
items.name: agree

items.doc: Scrub: candidate c's test passes on trunk, as trusted code observed it (index -1).
items.name: passes_on_trunk

items.doc: Candidate i of search k may land on trunk: a code or compaction candidate once a counterexample search on it cleared; a scrub candidate when its test passes on trunk. (intents 13, 21)
items.name: landable

items.doc: a at index ai outranks b at index bi: rank, then smaller diff, then earlier. (intent 5)
items.name: beats

items.doc: Code or compaction: index i is selected. (intents 4, 5, 17)
items.name: selected

items.doc: What a counterexample's test runs on: t's verified candidates, and for a compaction search its goal, as index -1. The goal is measured, not a voter.
items.name: member

items.doc: Counterexample: x's test splits the members of t. A test with no result on a member counts as splitting. (intents 13, 17)
items.name: splits

items.doc: Counterexample: some verified candidate of x splits t.
items.name: found

items.doc: Counterexample: every agent process of x returned, and no verified test splits t.
items.name: cleared

items.doc: Map: verified candidate i cites cue q.
items.name: cites

items.doc: Map: at least two verified candidates cite q. (intent 10)
items.name: agreed

items.doc: Map: exactly one verified candidate cites q. Shown to engineer apart from the proposal.
items.name: contested

items.doc: Map: w is the proposal's wording for q: the shortest among the citing candidates, ties to the earliest. (intent 10)
items.name: proposed

items.doc: Where a search's candidates start: always trunk's head. A counterexample's test is written from the spec and the intent, never from candidate code. (intent 22)
items.name: start

items.doc: The agent processes of search k: one per index.
items.name: agent_processes

items.doc: The capabilities grant adds: one per agent process, each with the search's authority and limit.
items.name: granted

items.doc: engineer committed to trunk, e.g. the map or the checks. (intent 6)
items.name: advance

items.doc: Open a search and grant one capability per agent process, reserving each one's limit. One search runs at a time; its agent processes run in parallel. (intents 2, 7, 9, 10, 13, 16, 17)
items.name: grant

items.doc: The bon process waits on an agent process and records what it returned and what it cost, consuming its capability and settling its limit. (OSTEP: wait) (intents 2, 7, 16)
items.name: wait

items.doc: Code or compaction: trunk fast-forwards to the selected candidate, if a counterexample search on it cleared and trunk hasn't moved. (intents 6, 13)
items.name: fast_forward

items.doc: Scrub: trunk retains the selected test when it passes on trunk and trunk hasn't moved. (intent 21)
items.name: retain

items.doc: What's selected is verified: exec code can rely on this.
items.name: selection_verified

items.doc: Each capability is held by an agent process for one open index of the running search, with that search's base, authority and limit. (intent 7)
items.name: capability_open

items.doc: Every agent process of every search has either returned or still holds its capability.
items.name: accounted

items.doc: Nothing spends past its limit: what is reserved is exactly the limits of the outstanding capabilities. (intent 16)
items.name: within_limit

items.doc: Candidates of a search are siblings of its base. (intent 2)
items.name: siblings

items.doc: Every trunk commit authored by agent is exactly a selected, landable candidate of a search on the previous head. (intents 3–6, 13, 21)
items.name: trunk_exact
